recipes.name: Millionaire Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Combine condensed milk and cream cheese in a large bowl; gently fold in whipped topping. Stir in crushed pineapple and pecans.
Divide filling among pie crusts. Chill in the refrigerator until set, 3 to 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Millionaire Pie
raw_recipe.description: This easy millionaire pie recipe features Cool Whip and cream cheese mixed with pineapple, pecans, and condensed milk over a graham cracker crust.

video.description: Your summer cookout isn’t complete without this rich and creamy dessert! In this video, Nicole shows you how to make a budget-friendly, no bake millionaire pie. Loaded with fresh pineapple taste and crunchy pecans, millionaire pie is decadent and super easy to throw together.

review.reviewBody: Yummie. When I tasted this before pouring it into the shells it tasted too sweet to me. I found another nearly identical recipe for this pie that called for 3 T of lemon juice. That addition made it PERFECT. Also, don't just drain - strain your pineapple a bit. Those that complained about this not setting up likely got pineapple juice into the pie.
My mother has beenn making this for years. It is great! I also add about a cup of mini-chocolate chips in mine. Excellent.
I love this recipe. My aunt used to make it at Christmas and add chopped up marachino cherries and chopped pecans.

Thank you so much for the recipe! I followed it exactly and the pies came out great. Be sure to FOLD in the whipped topping - if you put it in a mixer, it will turn to goo (as I have found in the past). That's probably why others have had trouble with it being runny. I will make these again & again!

After reading all the reviews and the preceding blog post, I opted to make a few changes to the recipe as a whole. Namely, I: 1. Used a homemade grahams cracker crust and made a deep dish pie, using the leftover filling to make two gluten-free pudding cups. 2. Added lime juice and lime zest from 3 limes to both thicken the filling and add some tartness to cut through all the sweet 3. Added chopped homemade amaretto cherries and some chopped Trader Joe’s Sweet n Spicy Pecans 4. Added a tablespoon of vanilla extract and a teaspoon of coconut extract (I was out of shredded coconut, but still wanted the flavor) 5. Use canned pineapple chunks that I drained, pulsed in a food processor, then drained again The flavor is pretty great, but next time I want to add some rum extract for more of a Mai Tai vibe. It’s also not the *prettiest* pie, but the flavor more than makes up for it. Next time I’ll use a full extra tub of whipped topping and some toasted coconut for the top.

delish... I am 82 years young I have been making this pie for as long as I can remember I made it as a teenager, years younger i t hink lol... I have a few add on if you are interested, like Christmas we put crushed peppermint candy on top before serving also chocolate chips in the batter, melted Werther's candy drizzled on top as served, m&Ms in the batter, strawberries candied on top as served, sweethearts just do your thing, have fun make it a trillion $$$ pie hugs all! This recipe needs several tablespoons of lemon juice to make the pie set. There are many variations using various fruits, some without the cream cheese (my mother's didn't have the cream cheese), but they use lemon juice to make the sweetened condensed milk set. 5 stars with the lemon juice. It is very rich (millionaire)! Especially good made with drained canned peaches, with or without pineapple, too.

Wow, I used to make this pie every Christmas, then lost the recipe and here it is, AMAZING. Instead of the crushed pineapple I was using a can of mix fruit salad 28 oz and very important to add 1/4 cup lemon juice which you mix with the condensed mild, the just add the other ingredients SUPER PIE.....EUMMMMM

Very easy and pretty tasty. Could use a little something zippy in the mix, but I'm not sure what. A lady at work makes hers with crushed mandarin oranges but I didn't want to stray from the original recipe yet. 

I do like that I get 2 pies from the recipe. I threw one in the freezer and took it to a New Year's lunch two weeks after I made them and it tasted great!

I needed a quickie recipe for dessert and had all the ingredients for these pies. I did follow the recipe though. Except I also added about 1/4 cup of shredded coconut and followed a reviewer's suggestion of adding 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. I also would make sure to drain/strain the pineapple, then drying it completely on a kitchen towel or paper towel before putting in the cream cheese mixture. It makes a huge difference! It didn't set fast enough for me, so I put the pies in the freezer for a couple of hours. I do suggest, however, to take it out and put in fridge before serving. It was a good pie. I liked the pie, but I will keep looking for another recipe like this.
Very good. Will make again and may add lemon or key lime juice to add a little more flavor
Love this pie, have been eating since I was a small child. Super good. So easy to make.
Didn't give ingredients just showed them dumped into bowl & mixed up.

A family member mentioned eating Millionaire Pie with fond memories .. So I decided to find a recipe and make it for her. It was just as she remembered it!!! She sliced and froze the remaining pie and was pleasantly surprised when she enjoyed it again a month later .. it freezes beautifully. Thank you for helping me make a fond memory a reality!

The only thing I do differently is put a maraschino cherry on each slice. I tried it with chopped ones blended in but this recipe is perfect without cherries. The cherry on top of each slice makes it pop when I take a picture of our holiday table. 😊
It was easy to make very tasty
